bug_semantics: LiquidJS strip_html returned attacker-controlled HTML tags containing CR or LF instead of tag-stripped text. A payload such as therefore reached an unescaped HTML response, where browsers treat the line terminators as attribute whitespace and execute the event handler. In the advisory-era implementation the immediate defect was the generic <.*?> alternative: JavaScript dot did not consume CR/LF, while the other multiline alternatives used [\s\S].
flaw_origin: Commit 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2 first added strip_html with /<\/?\s*\w+\s*\/?>/g. That filter already returned the advisory's executable newline-and-attribute payload unchanged; its immediate parent had no strip_html at all. Commit 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887 later replaced the original expression with the Ruby-Liquid-style alternatives and first wrote the advisory-era <.*?> implementation, but it did not introduce the vulnerability: the same payload and XSS trust path were already present in its parent. It changed the mechanism from a regex that rejected all attributed tags to one that handled same-line attributed tags but still rejected multiline ones.
ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file commit 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2` shows one parent, human author and committer harttle <yangjvn@126.com>, the message `filters: all`, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: The assigned GHSA-2qv6-9wx5-cwv4 bundle defines the exploit as strip_html returning a CR/LF-bearing executable tag, records affected liquidjs <=10.25.7, references fix 26ea2856c7a90aec892b98d94a9b7a3e18539045, and names v10.26.0 as the fix release.

The primary/reviewer disagreement was 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887 with parent f668a5cc4188c4b2ad82c0dbcdd31e6e5bb95aae versus 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2 with parent b478c798fdd5aba96b1fa279dd78410d4844584c. `git rev-parse <candidate>^` confirmed both claimed immediate parents.

`git show --format=fuller --patch 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2 -- filters.js` shows a normal one-parent source commit directly adding `strip_html` with /<\/?\s*\w+\s*\/?>/g; it is not a move, import, revert, or decomposed squash. `git show b478c798fdd5aba96b1fa279dd78410d4844584c:filters.js` shows the direct parent ends at escape_once and has no strip_html filter or vulnerable path.

A direct Node execution of the historical expressions against `` and `` produced, respectively: original regex = both inputs unchanged; 8e9e10 regex = same-line input empty but newline input unchanged; fixed regex = both inputs empty. This resolves introducer_sha in the reviewer's favor: the 8e9e10 parent was already exploitable by the advisory payload, so 8e9e10 only changed the regex mechanism and cannot be the first vulnerability-introducing commit.

`git show --patch 8e9e10fdb4c7f00ffa3997d3e2c0a0bfa48ce887 -- filters.js` confirms the primary's candidate replaced the already-bypassable original expression with `<script.*?</script>|<!--.*?-->|<style.*?</style>|<.*?>`. The primary correctly identified the first writer of the current catch-all line, but its parent-absence claim applies only to that syntax, not to the vulnerability behavior required by the direct-parent check.

`git tag --contains 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2 --sort=v:refname` begins at v1.2.0 and includes v3.1.2, whereas tags containing 8e9e10 begin at v3.1.3. The earlier boundary matches the bundle's unbounded-lower affected range `<= 10.25.7` and confirms that the flaw predates the primary candidate.

`git show` of direct member b976669ad3b21ad37c8aa2af3ef5709e2a58fe35 and advisory landing commit 26ea2856c7a90aec892b98d94a9b7a3e18539045 shows the same two-file security delta: `<.*?>` becomes `<[\s\S]*?>` and LF/CR/SVG regression cases are added. The direct member is therefore direct_fix_sha and the referenced landing commit is fix_sha.

Release ancestry checks with `git merge-base` returned 34877950bfd0f88666f4ef61f7704defdea546b0 for fix versus v10.25.7, so the fix is not an ancestor there, and returned the fix SHA itself for v10.26.0, proving the patched boundary.

BIC-only attribution comes from `git cat-file commit 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2`; the later Cursor trailer on the 2026 fix was excluded because fix-only AI evidence cannot classify the 2016 introducer.
reasoning: The reviewer wins both disputed fields. Vulnerability-first adjudication follows the executable behavior, not only blame for the line eventually edited by the fix. Commit 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2 created strip_html and immediately allowed the advisory payload through, while direct parent b478c798fdd5aba96b1fa279dd78410d4844584c had no filter. The primary's 8e9e10 candidate is the smallest commit that wrote the later `<.*?>` syntax, but its immediate parent returns the identical newline XSS payload; consequently it is a mechanism change, not the causal BIC. The v1.2.0 containing-tag boundary further rejects a v3.1.3 introduction. The vulnerability persisted through the later regex form until b976669ad3b21ad37c8aa2af3ef5709e2a58fe35 supplied the direct patch and 26ea2856c7a90aec892b98d94a9b7a3e18539045 landed it for v10.26.0. The resolved BIC commit object contains no AI signal, so the gate-complete verdict is NOT_AI.
